title: A tensor power satisfies the square condition on a smooth group over a normal base
statement: Let $S$ be an affine locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] whose local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $H\to S$ be a smooth separated morphism of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with an $S$-group scheme structure and connected fibres $H_s=H\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-connected-scheme]. An $S$-group scheme means a scheme $H$ with $S$-morphisms $m:H\times_SH\to H$, $i:H\to H$, $e:S\to H$ satisfying associativity, identity and inverse identities; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_H$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For an $S$-scheme $X$ with an $H$-action and an invertible module $M$ on $X$, use the following square condition. For any $S$-scheme $B$, put $X_B=X\times_SB$, with structure map $q_B:X_B\to B$, and let $M_B$ be the tensor pullback of $M$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. For $g\in H(B)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(B,H)$ let $\tau_g:X_B\to X_B$ be the action $x\mapsto gx$. Say that $M$ satisfies the square condition for this action if, for every such $B$ and every $g,h\in H(B)$, there is an invertible $\mathcal O_B$-module $N$ and an isomorphism $$\tau_{gh}^*M_B\otimes M_B\cong\tau_g^*M_B\otimes\tau_h^*M_B\otimes q_B^*N.$$ All tensors are module sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. This is equality of the translation differences in the group of invertible-module classes modulo modules pulled back from $B$; no coherence or chosen isomorphisms are part of the condition. For the left multiplication action on $X=H$, there exists an integer $r\geq1$ such that $M=L^{\otimes r}$ satisfies this square condition. The base $S$ need not be integral or connected, and $H$ need not be commutative or proper.

proof.text: First the fibres of $H\to S$ are geometrically integral. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-section-component-geometrically-irreducible] to $H\to S$ and its identity section $e$. Finite presentation gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness as in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The resulting open $U$ contains every point of the connected component through $e(s)$ in every fibre. Since $H_s$ is connected and has the point $e(s)$, this component is the whole fibre, so $U=H$. Thus every $H_s$ is geometrically irreducible. By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] these fibres are also geometrically reduced, hence geometrically integral by the definitions [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme] (integral means reduced and irreducible).

source.place: Guo Proposition 5.9 final assertion, proof via Proposition 5.2 and the coordinate calculation of Lemma 5.7; online March 31, 2026 version.

proof.text: Because $S$ is affine it is quasi-compact: refine an open cover of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ by basic opens $D(f)$; the corresponding $f$ generate the unit ideal, and an expression for $1$ uses finitely many of them. Hence $S$ is Noetherian. Apply clause (2) of [rem-pc-regular-normal] to write $S=\coprod_{j\in J}S_j$ as a finite disjoint union of nonempty normal integral open and closed subschemes. If $J$ is empty, then $S=H=\varnothing$ and $r=1$ works, with the unique line on every (necessarily empty) $S$-scheme $B$. Otherwise work on each $S_j$. The restriction $H_j=H\times_SS_j\to S_j$ is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change] and of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. It remains separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change], as the base change of the separated morphism $H\to S$ along $S_j\to S$. Its fibres are the fibres of $H$ above points of $S_j$, hence geometrically integral by Step 1.

source.place: Guo Proposition 5.9 final assertion, proof via Proposition 5.2 and the coordinate calculation of Lemma 5.7; online March 31, 2026 version.

proof.text: Fix $j$. Set $X_1=X_2=X_3=H_j$, $C=H_j^3$, and let $a:C\to H_j$ be $a(u,v,x)=uv^{-1}x$. Put $A=a^*(L|_{H_j})$. Pullback preserves invertibility: a local generator of a rank-one locally free module pulls back to a local generator [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback]. At the generic point $\eta_j$ the three factors are smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change], still separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] and of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], both applied to the base change along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta_j)\to S_j$, and geometrically integral by Step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-field-product-square-power] to $A_{\eta_j}$. It gives $n_j\geq1$ for which $D(A_{\eta_j}^{\otimes n_j})$ is pulled back from $(H_{j,\eta_j})^4$. Pullback commutes with tensors and duals (check on local rank-one generators), so this is precisely the generic restriction of $D(A^{\otimes n_j})$.

source.place: Guo Proposition 5.9 final assertion, proof via Proposition 5.2 and the coordinate calculation of Lemma 5.7; online March 31, 2026 version.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-product-square-descent] over $S_j$, with its three factors $H_j$ and the line $A^{\otimes n_j}$. Normal integrality of $S_j$ is Step 2; smooth separated finite presentation and geometric integrality of all fibres were checked in Steps 1-2. The generic descent hypothesis is exactly Step 3. Consequently there is an invertible $N_j$ on $H_j^4$ and an isomorphism $D(A^{\otimes n_j})\cong\pi^*N_j$ on $H_j^4\times_{S_j}H_j$.

source.place: Guo Proposition 5.9 final assertion, proof via Proposition 5.2 and the coordinate calculation of Lemma 5.7; online March 31, 2026 version.

proof.text: Write $M_j=(L|_{H_j})^{\otimes n_j}$. For any $B\to S_j$ and $g,h\in H_j(B)$, pull the isomorphism of Step 4 back along $$H_{j,B}\longrightarrow H_j^4\times_{S_j}H_j,\qquad x\longmapsto(g,e,h^{-1},e,x).$$ In the coordinates $(u_0,u_1,v_0,v_1,x)$ defining $D$, the four composites with $a$ are, respectively, $ghx,x,gx,hx$ for $(00),(11),(01),(10)$. Thus its left side becomes $$\tau_{gh}^*M_{j,B}\otimes M_{j,B}\otimes(\tau_g^*M_{j,B})^{-1}\otimes(\tau_h^*M_{j,B})^{-1}.$$ The right side is $q_B^*(g,e,h^{-1},e)^*N_j$ by pullback composition [def-pc-module-pullback]. Tensor by $\tau_g^*M_{j,B}\otimes\tau_h^*M_{j,B}$ and cancel each line with its inverse [def-sc-invertible-module]. This is the required square identity, with $N=(g,e,h^{-1},e)^*N_j$. No factors in a group product have been commuted.

source.place: Guo Proposition 5.9 final assertion, proof via Proposition 5.2 and the coordinate calculation of Lemma 5.7; online March 31, 2026 version.

proof.text: Choose $r=\prod_{j\in J}n_j\geq1$. On $S_j$, tensor the isomorphism in Step 5 exactly $r/n_j$ times. Since pullback and tensor powers commute on local generators, it gives the square identity for $L^{\otimes r}|_{H_j}$ with base line $N^{\otimes(r/n_j)}$. For arbitrary $B\to S$, the inverse images $B_j=B\times_SS_j$ are a finite disjoint open and closed cover of $B$. Define the base line on each $B_j$ by this formula; its sheaf on $B$ assigns to an open $V$ the product of the section modules on $V\cap B_j$. This is locally a rank-one free module, and the component isomorphisms give an isomorphism on $H_B$ by the identical disjoint-cover construction. This proves the square condition for every $B,g,h$ with the single exponent $r$.
